hints: Look at what type of reaction a halogenoalkane undergoes with ammonia and with cyanide ions, both are nucleophilic substitution.
Reaction 1 replaces Br with an $\text{NH}_2$ group to give propylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$.
For reaction 2, remember that adding one carbon to make a nitrile that hydrolyses to butanoic acid needs $\text{CN}^-$ as a nucleophile in ethanol, not addition of HCN to a carbonyl.
walkthrough:
**Identify compound X from reaction 1**

Ammonia acts as a nucleophile towards the halogenoalkane. It replaces the bromine atom with an amino group.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + 2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{NH}_4\text{Br}$$

**Work backwards from butanoic acid to find Y**

Butanoic acid has 4 carbons, while 1-bromopropane has 3 carbons. So reaction 2 must add one carbon.

Hydrolysis link:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_3$$
So Y must be the nitrile $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ (butanenitrile).

**Choose the correct reagent to make the nitrile**

To make a nitrile from a halogenoalkane we need nucleophilic substitution by $\text{CN}^-$. This needs KCN (or NaCN) dissolved in ethanol, heated under reflux.

Reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Br}^-$$
Aqueous HCN is used for nucleophilic addition to aldehydes and ketones, not for substitution of halogenoalkanes. So X is propylamine and the reagent is KCN in ethanol.

options.A: Compound X is correctly given as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, but HCN(aq) is wrong for reaction 2. Aqueous HCN adds to carbonyl compounds (aldehydes and ketones), it does not substitute Br in a halogenoalkane to give a nitrile.
options.B: This is correct on both sides. Ammonia in ethanol substitutes Br to give propylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$. KCN dissolved in ethanol provides $\text{CN}^-$ for substitution to give butanenitrile, which hydrolyses to butanoic acid with one extra carbon.
options.C: Both parts are incorrect. Ammonia does not give an alcohol, aqueous NaOH would be needed for $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Also HCN(aq) is for addition to C=O, not for converting a bromoalkane into a nitrile.
options.D: The reagent KCN in ethanol is correct for making the nitrile Y, but compound X is wrong. Heating with ammonia gives the amine $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, not the alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
